result.tests: 831 passed, 10 skipped, 1 xfailed, 14 warnings in 129.30s (0:02:09) -- full `pytest tests/ -q` on AlphaCube-steering after the WP9 commit. Baseline was 617/10/1; pass count only increased (the extra passes come from WP1/2/3/5/6's own already-committed tests plus WP9's 22 new tests), 0 failures, skip/xfail counts unchanged. The WP9 file alone (`pytest tests/test_build_daily_fields.py -q`) is 22 passed in <1s.
deviations: No prior WP9 commit existed (checked via `git log --oneline -40` before starting), so this was a full implementation, not a skip-and-verify.

FloatShares's source column name: the design pins FloatCap/TotalCap's exact columns but, by its own wording, leaves the share-count column unnamed ('a share column if one exists'). No production parquet schema was reachable this session to confirm a real name, so I added SHARE_COLUMN_CANDIDATES -- a documented, best-effort guess among common vendor spellings -- and record whichever one (if any) actually matched in meta.json's columns_used, so the choice is auditable. This is the one place the implementation is genuinely guessing rather than following a pinned fact; flagged in both the script's module docstring and the test file's docstring.

write_daily_field_store extends the literal 'write into a temp directory ... and os.replace it into place' (step 7): POSIX rename/os.replace cannot atomically swap a directory onto an existing NON-EMPTY directory (verified empirically). Rather than silently shutil.rmtree-ing a stale --out first, I made it fail loudly with a clear SystemExit naming the path, leaving any pre-existing --out completely untouched. Covered by test_rerunning_against_an_existing_nonempty_out_refuses_rather_than_overwriting. This is a safety-motivated extension beyond the literal spec text, not a contradiction of it -- flagging it so a reviewer can override if a different rebuild policy is wanted.

Added a call to dailyfields.require_board_rule(store.symbols) inside main(), which is NOT in WP9's own numbered step list (1-9) or test bullets, but IS explicitly named in dailyfields.py's own (already-merged, WP2) docstring for require_board_rule as one of exactly two required call sites ('the daily-source attach ... and scripts/build_daily_fields.py next to its coverage floor'). Since this script opens the store with no daily_root (there is nothing to attach yet -- that is what is being built), the automatic check inside CubeStore/SegmentedCubeStore's daily-attach path never fires here, so without this explicit call a store whose full symbol list is in the old non-digit-first format would go uncaught. Covered by test_a_store_whose_symbols_can_never_match_a_board_rule_is_refused.

Wrote both new files in English (docstrings and comments), matching the already-merged sibling files this package depends on most directly (dailyfields.py, synthetic.py, test_daily_fields_store.py, test_daily_leaf_typing.py -- all WP1-3, all English), even though the broader scripts/ and tests/ directories are predominantly Chinese-commented. This is a style judgment call, not a correctness one; flagging in case the reviewer prefers the directory's majority convention instead.

--dry-run's exact semantics are not specified beyond being listed as a flag. Implemented as: run every validation and build the planes in memory (so the --min-coverage gate fires exactly as a real run would, for an accurate preview), but skip the final write+rename. Covered by two tests I added on my own judgment (test_dry_run_writes_nothing_but_still_runs_the_coverage_gate, test_dry_run_still_exits_nonzero_below_the_coverage_floor).

probe_schema's fallback when no store date has a matching parquet file (picks the earliest filename in --cap-dir by sorted glob) is my own reasonable choice, not specified by the design; covered by test_probe_schema_falls_back_to_a_directory_listing_when_no_date_matches.

No edit was needed outside the two owned files (scripts/build_daily_fields.py, tests/test_build_daily_fields.py) -- unlike some other packages, WP9's design did not require touching any file outside its ownership list.
result.notes:
Public names introduced, all in scripts/build_daily_fields.py (nothing else in the repo imports this script, confirmed by grep before writing, so there is no backward-compat surface to protect beyond internal consistency):
- Module constants: SYMBOL_COLUMN, CAP_COLUMN ('circulating_market_value'), TOTAL_COLUMN ('total_market_value'), SHARE_COLUMN_CANDIDATES (tuple, see deviations), REQUIRED_COLUMNS, FIELD_COLUMN.
- Functions: refuse_if_out_inside_sources(out_dir, cap_dir, store_dir) -> None [raises SystemExit]; probe_schema(cap_dir, dates) -> (Path, List[str] columns, List[str] symbols) [raises SystemExit if cap_dir has no parquet reachable]; choose_columns(columns, only) -> Dict[field_name, column_name] [raises SystemExit on an unknown --only name or a missing required column]; build_planes(symbols, dates, cap_dir, columns_used) -> Dict[field_name, (S,D) float64 ndarray]; summarize(planes, dates) -> (coverage Dict[str,float], date_range Dict[str, Optional[Tuple[str,str]]]); write_daily_field_store(out_dir, planes, symbols, dates, meta_extra) -> Path [raises SystemExit if out_dir already exists non-empty]; main(argv=None) -> int.
- meta.json is a strict superset of what DailyFieldStore.__init__ actually reads (fields/symbols/dates, plus n_symbols/n_days) -- the extra audit keys (source_paths, built_at, columns_used, coverage, date_range) are ignored by DailyFieldStore but let WP10/WP11 or an operator later audit exactly which parquet column fed FloatShares on a given server run, which matters given the share-column-name deviation above.
- The hard backward-compatibility requirement from the environment instructions (no new argument may consume an extra self._rng draw) is inapplicable to this package: build_daily_fields.py and its test are both brand-new files that touch no existing RNG-consuming code path (TypedTreeGenerator, GPMiner, etc.) at all; I verified via grep that nothing pre-existing references this script, so there is nothing to be bit-identical with.
- Least-confident spot for a future reviewer: SHARE_COLUMN_CANDIDATES's exact spellings are an informed guess, not a verified fact (no server access this session). If the real production schema turns out to use a name not in that tuple, FloatShares will simply and silently not be built (by design -- never synthesized), which is the correct failure mode, but the operator should check the printed 'columns: [...]' schema-probe line on the first real server run and add the real name to the tuple if it's missing.
- I did not touch requirements.txt: pandas.read_parquet needs pyarrow, which is already installed in ~/.venvs/alphacube and already a de facto dependency of scripts/tearsheet.py (whose load_caps this script's column-reading logic deliberately mirrors).
- I did not wire this script into src/alphacube/cli.py or any pipeline entry point -- WP9's file-ownership list covers exactly the two files touched, and nothing in the design's WP9 section calls for CLI/pipeline wiring beyond the script's own argparse.
- Scratch/experiment work for this package (a few empirical one-off checks of numpy/os.replace/pandas-parquet semantics, run inline via heredocs, nothing persisted) left no files; my designated scratch subdirectory /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/wp9-sonnet/ exists but is empty.
